previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior stents, was admitted for shortness of breath and chest pain lasting three days. Initial evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with negative troponins and unchanged EKG. Chest X-ray and clinical findings indicated an exacerbation of diastolic heart failure, confirmed by elevated JVP and pulmonary crackles. He was treated with IV furosemide, later transitioned to oral diuretics, with improvement in symptoms and radiographic findings. His Toprol XL was increased to 150 mg daily for better angina and heart failure control. Anemia was noted, likely microcytic and chronic, and iron supplementation was initiated with docusate for constipation prevention. His home medications for diabetes, including metformin, were restarted. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled for lab monitoring and ongoing management of heart failure, coronary disease, and anemia.
